solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: My word! One's dropped a low type

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left out, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: parole is a word of honour, as in giving one's word
A as the indefinite article means one

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at seeing a lowly person brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: PAROLE loses its A to leave PROLE. 'My word!' reads as an exclamation but is a word of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Prole, short for proletarian, is a dismissive name for a working-class person of humble status.

clue.text: see 23ac.
Ex-president loused up — toerag!

indicators.note: something loused up is botched and messed about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a former head of state who made a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A toerag is British slang for a contemptible person. Daniel Ortega led Nicaragua in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega was a former president of Nicaragua, so he is an example of an ex-president.

clue.text: Mouth part of familiar Peter almost spluttering bile

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is cut

parts.note: Mandy is the familiar nickname of Labour politician Peter Mandelson

indicators.note: spluttering speech comes out garbled and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter Mandelson sputters venom from his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson, the Labour spin doctor, was widely nicknamed Mandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the jawbone, a part of the mouth in humans and other animals.

clue.text: Row associated with bad economic times

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a queue of people waiting for handouts of food

definitions.note: the answer here is a noun used in phrases like 'on the breadline'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the level of poverty linked with hard times

explanation.surface: A quarrel linked with a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is a line of people queueing.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadline is both a queue for free food and the poverty threshold that hard times push people towards.

clue.text: Hint: he's playing with it, so likely to be punished?

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters of hint and he's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip that someone fooling around will end up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: HINTHES rearranged gives INTHESH, then IT unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: In the shit is vulgar slang meaning in serious trouble and facing blame.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Tonto's homilies full of bullshit

indicators.note: the words are full of the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the start of the next

explanation.surface: The Lone Ranger's sidekick Tonto preaches nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is a British word for nonsense or rubbish talk, a milder synonym of the crude term.

clue.text: Endless diarrhoea after hearing rehearsal

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second in the answer

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: the runs is slang for diarrhoea

explanation.surface: Someone with persistent diarrhoea after a court appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a test performance before the real thing, which is what a rehearsal is.

clue.text: What's Labour supposed to do, finished, trapped by Gordon's extremes?

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it
the extremes of a word are its very first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of the name
over means finished

explanation.surface: A jibe that Labour, a finished party under Gordon Brown, was failing at its job.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Labour prime minister when this was set; the definition asks what a governing party should do.
explanation.definitionFit: A party in power is supposed to rule the country, which is what governing means.

clue.text: Duff ITV pollster left right out of stalemate election

indicators.note: duff is British slang for useless or broken, so these letters are rearranged
out of means removed from, so those letters are taken from pollster

explanation.surface: A useless TV pollster has called an indecisive election wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLSTER without L and R is POLSTE, rearranged with ITV.
explanation.definitionFit: A split vote divides support between candidates, so no clear winner emerges, a deadlocked result.

clue.text: (& 7ac.) As the terrorist posed in hard hat, teeth 80% rotten?

indicators.note: rotten means decayed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
80% of a five-letter word is its first four letters

explanation.surface: A terrorist wearing a hard hat, with badly decayed teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 80% of TEETH is TEET; with HARDHAT, these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A death threat is a menace to kill someone, the kind a terrorist issues.

clue.text: Ex-political commentator chappie nuts for our selection of boobs

parts.note: John Cole was the BBC's political editor in the 1980s
a chappie is a man
nuts and balls are both slang for testicles

explanation.surface: A former pundit goes crazy over Private Eye's collection of blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is Private Eye speaking: Colemanballs is its long-running column of broadcasters' verbal gaffes, named after sports commentator David Coleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs are blunders, and the magazine's Colemanballs column collects spoken gaffes sent in by readers.

clue.text: Entrance of Cameron's "flock": Hull sadly left out, stuffed

indicators.note: an entrance is a way in, so the first letter of Cameron's
sadly means in a sorry state, so the flock and hull letters are rearranged
out means taken away, so the left letter is removed from Hull

explanation.surface: David Cameron's Tory faithful, with Hull sadly excluded, packed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull, an English city, loses an L, giving HUL; that and FLOCK are rearranged after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chock-full means filled to capacity, crammed or packed full.

clue.text: Bollocks location for some Crufts entrants — don't expect them to win

definitions.text: Bollocks location for some Crufts entrants
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: where a male show dog's testicles hang, beneath the animal
second meaning: competitors not tipped to succeed

explanation.surface: A crude joke about dog-show contestants that nobody tips for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's big annual dog show; read as two words, the answer says where a dog's testicles are.
explanation.definitionFit: Underdogs are competitors thought likely to lose, so nobody expects them to come out on top.

clue.text: Hard one, Brown, clutching $1000 piece

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an means one

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it tightly within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
a grand, a thousand dollars, is G

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, a tough man, grasping a thousand dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like Gordon Brown but is the colour dun, which holds G.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a gun, especially a handgun carried by a criminal.

clue.text: Ben Elton's work, earning him lots of money for jam!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1991 novel by the comedian Ben Elton
second meaning: a traffic jam that brings streets to a standstill

explanation.surface: Ben Elton's writing made him rich for very little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money for jam' is a British idiom for easy money, but 'jam' stands alone as the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridlock is a complete traffic standstill, which is what a traffic jam is.

clue.text: Canine screwed up eating hot Madras once

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so a letter goes in the middle
something screwed up is twisted and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A dog gets sick after eating a hot curry.
explanation.walkthrough: Madras looks like the curry, but it is the Indian city renamed in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Chennai is the current name of the Indian city formerly called Madras.

clue.text: Piss-poor Conservative game

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A dismissal of the Tories' tactics as pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or of very low quality, like the vulgar term.

clue.text: Acknowledgement by champ: chances of advancement crappy in this state

definitions.text: chances of advancement crappy in this state

parts.note: credit is acknowledgement given for something
to champ is to chew noisily, or crunch

explanation.surface: A boxing champion thanks people while lamenting poor career prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb meaning to chomp.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit crunch is a sudden shortage of lending in which economic prospects for advancement collapse.

clue.text: Left and Right, etc. involved with a red

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Politicians of every stripe getting entangled with a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A red' suggests a communist, but red is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, and the word is also a shade of red.

clue.text: Unauthentic, dodgy — eff off and be systematic!

definitions.note: the answer is a verb meaning to arrange systematically

parts.note: cod is British informal for fake or mock

indicators.note: off means taken away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: iffy means dodgy or doubtful
eff is the name of the letter F

explanation.surface: An angry outburst telling a phoney to clear off and get organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff off' reads as a mild swear, but eff is the spelt-out letter, removed once from IFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To codify is to arrange rules or laws into an orderly system.

clue.text: see 22dn.
(& 21dn.) The old PM (vacillating oily brat) welcomes aboard Mandelson finally

indicators.note: welcoming aboard takes an extra letter into the mix before it is stirred
vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters shift about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A dig at a wavering, slick former prime minister bringing Peter Mandelson back into government.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was Labour prime minister from 1997 to 2007, a former holder of the office.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Flirted so crappily, holding back Bill, the ex-president

indicators.note: back means read backwards, right to left
holding takes the extra piece into the mixture of letters
done crappily means done badly and messily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's clumsy flirting with a former head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests Clinton, but it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was Cuba's leader and president until 2008, so a former president.

clue.text: Protected species of dildo alarm going off — date scarpers

indicators.note: going off means sounding or exploding, so the letters are rearranged
scarpers is British slang for runs away, so the date letter leaves dildo

explanation.surface: A sex toy sets off an alarm, so the date flees.
explanation.walkthrough: DILDO loses a D, giving ILDO, which is rearranged with ALARM.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal; some kinds are listed as protected wildlife.

clue.text: They're left to stick a swizzle of ice in members

indicators.note: to stick something in somewhere is to put it inside

parts.note: legs are limbs, also called members
taken as written

indicators.note: a swizzle is a stirring, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bar instructions for putting a swizzle-stirred drink with ice into members' glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're left' reads as people remaining, but legacies are what is left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Legacies are gifts bequeathed in a will, things left to heirs after a death.

clue.text: Sort of guy ignited by extremists?

definitions.text: Sort of guy ignited by extremists?

parts.words: Sort of guy ignited by extremists?
parts.note: surface reading: a man set alight by radicals; setter's reading: a Guy, the stuffed figure burnt on Bonfire Night commemorating the extremist Guy Fawkes

explanation.walkthrough: On 5 November British bonfires burn a 'guy', a stuffed dummy of the Gunpowder Plotter Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bonfire Night guy is a stuffed model of a person, which is a kind of crude likeness made to be burnt.
